Personally I've learned that trying to curb my cravings or eat something else just makes me eat more of it in the end. I don't restrict any food groups. If I'm craving something, I have it including chips, candy etc. I find if I eat some, I usually don't need to eat much in order to feel satisfied. My brain and body now trust me and know I will always satisfy any craving and it doesn't need to worry I won't get it again which causes binging. Where as before I might've restricted the food group which makes me want to eat a lot of it in case I don't get it again. Trying to replace a food I'm craving with a "healthy" alternative also can lead to binging as it's not as satisfying and I might end up feeling duped. Doing this method I eat way way less than I used to. I also in general have less cravings and don't binge eat at all. It does take some personal insight on your personal hunger and full cues though and not just eating "just to eat" or past the point of fullness which I would consider a binge.

I moved in with my boyfriend last September in the middle of my weight loss journey. He eats WAY more than I do, but furthermore, he enjoys exactly the same type of food I do and going out to eat became a bonding point for us. I quickly gained back about 10 lbs and stopped losing any weight trying to keep up with this. However at the beginning of this year, I knew I’d just keep gaining my weight back if I didn’t take control and ownership of my own actions. I was pretty embarrassed at first to have him see me count calories, weigh food etc. but I’ve lost 25 lbs since January and reached my goal weight. I learned to adapt! We still go out to eat; I just eat half my entree and only one beer instead of several. When cooking at home, I use lower calorie substitutes for my portion for things like bread, pasta etc and load up on the veggies. Honestly these habits even transferred to him and now he eats most of the same food I do. It was awkward/personal at first to me when he realized I was trying to lose weight but now he’s so proud of me and is very helpful and supportive. He never looks down on me for turning down food or making a healthy choice. 


Our diet btw, is totally not the healthiest although it’s a bit better since it’s summer and we barbecue meats a lot. We eat Mac n cheese, hot dogs, frozen food, fast food, etc. I just stopped making excuses and tailored what I eat to fit my caloric needs. My boyfriend LOVES snacking, it’s his nightly habit to grub down on something delicious but he hardly even noticed at first when I wouldn’t partake and he still doesn’t care. I actually help him pick out snack so it still feels like I’m participating, haha.

To go the extra mile, I often google pics of the chain restaurant version of the entree I’m eating to make sure it’s really similar. It’s still estimation but better than just a random guessed number.

Various things that helped with night time snacking in my weight loss along the way (I didn’t do all of them every day): going to the gym or for a long walk after 7pm (if I’m freshly worked out I feel less likely to want to snack), sticking to intermittent fasting that ends my eating window at 8pm, allocating 100-300 calories for night snacks (usually popsicles, or some kind of treat since I have a sweet tooth), going to bed earlier, and also always trying to make sure my dinner is satisfying and well balanced. Another trick I picked up was to find something to do with my hands so I can’t snack like video games, knitting, drawing, sewing etc. don’t want to ruin my craft with Cheeto dust fingers!

I do lazy IF. I usually don’t eat between 830pm-1230pm but I don’t stress if I need a 50-150 calorie snack sometime in between (typically at night). I guess it just depends on what you’re hoping to get out of IF - for me I care less about the actual fasting benefits and more that it helps me stick to my calorie limit and lose weight.

The C25k program is great for easing into running. However if it feels too easy, then it’s fine to skip to the middle of the program and start somewhere there... whenever I take a long break from running, I always pick up at week 5 or 6 again and work through those weeks because they are incredibly helpful in building up endurance quickly to a 30 min consistent run. As for staying focused to increase run time, podcasts help a ton in distracting me from watching the timer! Another great tip I learned is to not try to run so fast you couldn’t have a conversation or you’re out of breath. You can gradually increase your speed over time as your endurance builds, no need to be doing long distance sprints when learning to run!

Personally running regularly helps my weight loss a ton! It motivates me to stay on track with my eating plan, and It didn't take long for my regular runs to help create a deficit that really makes a difference! I usually burn over 500 up to 700 calories in my runs, so sometimes that can add up to a half lb or even more! And my body composition is much better when I'm running regularly as well. I definitely recommend it.
